source.text: Ἀδελφοί, ἡ μὲν εὐδοκία τῆς ἐμῆς καρδίας καὶ ἡ δέησις πρὸς τὸν θεὸν ὑπὲρ αὐτῶν εἰς σωτηρίαν.

records.literal_gloss: Brothers, the indeed desire of the my heart and the prayer to the God on behalf of them [is] for salvation.

en.L: {{gender:Brothers and sisters|Brothers}}, the desire of my heart and [my] prayer to God for them [is] for [their] salvation.
en.B: {{gender:Brothers and sisters|Brothers}}, what my heart longs for, and what I ask God for them, is that they may be saved.
en.R: {{gender:Brothers and sisters|Brothers}}, I long with all my heart for my people Israel to be saved. That is what I pray to God for them.

es.L: Hermanos, el deseo de mi corazón y [mi] oración a Dios por ellos [es] para [su] salvación.
es.B: Hermanos, lo que mi corazón anhela, y lo que pido a Dios por ellos, es que sean salvos.
es.R: Hermanos, deseo con todo mi corazón que mi pueblo, Israel, sea salvo. Eso es lo que pido a Dios por ellos.

sw.L: Ndugu, shauku ya moyo wangu na maombi [yangu] kwa Mungu kwa ajili yao [ni] kwa ajili ya wokovu [wao].
sw.B: Ndugu, kile ambacho moyo wangu unatamani, na kile ninachomwomba Mungu kwa ajili yao, ni kwamba waokolewe.
sw.R: Ndugu, ninatamani kwa moyo wangu wote kwamba watu wa taifa langu, Israeli, waokolewe. Hilo ndilo ninalomwomba Mungu kwa ajili yao.

fr.L: {{gender:Frères et sœurs|Frères}}, le désir de mon cœur et [ma] prière à Dieu pour eux, [c’est] pour [leur] salut.
fr.B: {{gender:Frères et sœurs|Frères}}, ce que mon cœur désire et ce que je demande à Dieu pour eux, c’est qu’ils soient sauvés.
fr.R: {{gender:Frères et sœurs|Frères}}, je désire de tout mon cœur que mon peuple, Israël, soit sauvé. C’est ce que je demande à Dieu pour eux.

ko.L: {{gender:형제자매|형제}} 여러분, 내 마음의 소원과 그들을 위하여 하나님께 [드리는 나의] 간구는 [그들의] 구원을 위한 것입니다.
ko.B: {{gender:형제자매|형제}} 여러분, 내가 마음으로 간절히 바라고 그들을 위해 하나님께 구하는 것은 그들이 구원받는 것입니다.
ko.R: {{gender:형제자매|형제}} 여러분, 나는 내 동족 이스라엘 백성이 구원받기를 온 마음으로 바랍니다. 나는 그들을 위해 하나님께 그렇게 기도합니다.

vi.L: Thưa {{gender:anh chị em|anh em}}, điều lòng tôi ao ước và lời cầu xin [của tôi] với Đức Chúa Trời cho họ là [để họ được] cứu rỗi.
vi.B: Thưa {{gender:anh chị em|anh em}}, điều lòng tôi hằng mong mỏi và điều tôi cầu xin Đức Chúa Trời cho họ là họ được cứu.
vi.R: Thưa {{gender:anh chị em|anh em}}, tôi hết lòng mong cho dân Y-sơ-ra-ên của tôi được cứu. Đó là điều tôi cầu xin Đức Chúa Trời cho họ.

decisions.choice: desire, what the heart longs for
decisions.reason: εὐδοκία can mean God's good pleasure or a person's goodwill, but beside "of my heart" and "prayer" it is Paul's own deep wish.

decisions.choice: "them" is the people of Israel who have not believed
alternatives: the Jews in general, believers included
decisions.reason: The pronoun looks back to Israel in 9:31-33, which pursued the law but stumbled over the stone. Paul's grief for them began in 9:1-3.

decisions.choice: the "on the one hand" has no matching "on the other"
decisions.reason: μὲν usually expects a contrasting clause with "but". None follows; the contrast is implied in verses 2-3, where Paul turns to what is wrong.

decisions.choice: my people Israel
decisions.reason: Readable names who "them" are (meaning note m2), since a new reader may start here.

decisions.choice: hermanos, no setting
decisions.reason: As in Romans 1:13, Spanish "hermanos" already covers brothers and sisters, so there is no gender span.

decisions.choice: ndugu, no setting
alternatives: ndugu wa kiume na wa kike
decisions.reason: As in Romans 1:13, "ndugu" already means brothers and sisters, so Swahili needs no gender span.

decisions.choice: 합쇼체 with "여러분" continues; "{{gender:형제자매|형제}} 여러분", as settled at 1:13; no deity_pronoun spans (as through the letter)
decisions.reason: As settled at 1:1: the letter is in 합쇼체 at every level. Korean has no deity_pronoun spans because there are no capital letters for the setting to change; respect for God and Christ is carried by -시- and 께서.

decisions.choice: "내 동족 이스라엘 백성" (R)
decisions.reason: Readable names the people meant, as the English Readable does (meaning decision: "them" is Israel).

decisions.choice: "dân Y-sơ-ra-ên của tôi" (R)
decisions.reason: "Them" is the people of Israel who have not believed (m2); Readable names them, as the English Readable does, since "họ" alone would leave the reader looking back to chapter 9.

source.text: μαρτυρῶ γὰρ αὐτοῖς ὅτι ζῆλον θεοῦ ἔχουσιν· ἀλλ’ οὐ κατ’ ἐπίγνωσιν, ἀγνοοῦντες γὰρ τὴν τοῦ θεοῦ δικαιοσύνην, καὶ τὴν ἰδίαν ζητοῦντες στῆσαι, τῇ δικαιοσύνῃ τοῦ θεοῦ οὐχ ὑπετάγησαν·

records.literal_gloss: I bear witness for to them that zeal of God they have; but not according to knowledge, \v 3 being ignorant of for the of the God righteousness, and the own seeking to establish, to the righteousness of the God not they submitted;

en.L: For I testify about them that they have zeal for God, but not according to knowledge. \v 3 For being ignorant of the righteousness of God, and seeking to establish [their] own, they did not submit to the righteousness of God.
en.B: I can vouch for them that they are eager for God, but their eagerness is not guided by real understanding. \v 3 They did not recognize the righteousness of God, and in trying to set up a righteousness of their own, they would not submit to the righteousness that comes from God.
en.R: I can tell you that they are very eager to serve God. But they do not really understand. \v 3 They did not know about the righteousness of God: how God puts people right with {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}. They tried to have a righteousness of their own instead. So they would not accept the righteousness God gives.

es.L: Porque doy testimonio de ellos de que tienen celo de Dios, pero no conforme a conocimiento. \v 3 Porque, desconociendo la justicia de Dios, y tratando de establecer la suya propia, no se sometieron a la justicia de Dios.
es.B: Puedo dar fe de que tienen celo por Dios, pero su celo no está guiado por un verdadero entendimiento. \v 3 No reconocieron la justicia de Dios, y al tratar de establecer una justicia propia, no quisieron someterse a la justicia que viene de Dios.
es.R: Yo sé bien que tienen muchas ganas de servir a Dios. Pero no entienden de verdad. \v 3 No conocían la justicia de Dios: cómo Dios pone a las personas en una relación correcta con {{deity_pronoun:él mismo|Él mismo}}. En cambio, trataron de tener una justicia propia. Por eso no quisieron aceptar la justicia que Dios da.

sw.L: Kwa maana ninatoa ushahidi kuwahusu kwamba wana bidii ya Mungu, lakini si kwa kufuata ufahamu. \v 3 Kwa sababu hawakuitambua haki ya Mungu, nao wakijitahidi kuweka [haki] yao wenyewe, hawakunyenyekea kwa haki ya Mungu.
sw.B: Ninaweza kuwathibitishia kwamba wana bidii kubwa kwa ajili ya Mungu, lakini bidii yao haiongozwi na ufahamu wa kweli. \v 3 Hawakuitambua haki ya Mungu, na kwa kujaribu kujiwekea haki yao wenyewe, walikataa kunyenyekea kwa haki inayotoka kwa Mungu.
sw.R: Naweza kushuhudia kwamba wana hamu kubwa ya kumtumikia Mungu. Lakini hawaelewi kweli. \v 3 Hawakujua kuhusu haki ya Mungu: jinsi Mungu anavyowaweka watu katika uhusiano mwema naye {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}}. Badala yake walijaribu kuwa na haki yao wenyewe. Kwa hiyo hawakukubali haki ambayo Mungu anaitoa.

fr.L: Car je leur rends ce témoignage qu’ils ont du zèle pour Dieu, mais non selon [la] connaissance. \v 3 Car, ignorant la justice de Dieu et cherchant à établir leur propre [justice], ils ne se sont pas soumis à la justice de Dieu.
fr.B: Je peux témoigner qu’ils ont du zèle pour Dieu, mais ce zèle n’est pas guidé par une vraie connaissance. \v 3 Ils n’ont pas reconnu la justice de Dieu, et en cherchant à établir une justice qui leur soit propre, ils ne se sont pas soumis à la justice qui vient de Dieu.
fr.R: Je peux vous le dire : ils sont pleins d’ardeur pour servir Dieu. Mais ils ne comprennent pas vraiment. \v 3 Ils n’ont pas connu la justice de Dieu, c’est-à-dire la façon dont Dieu rend les gens justes devant {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}. Ils ont plutôt essayé d’avoir leur propre justice. Alors ils n’ont pas voulu accepter la justice que Dieu donne.

ko.L: 나는 그들에 대하여 증언합니다. 그들에게는 하나님을 향한 열심이 있습니다. 그러나 [그것은] 지식을 따른 것이 아닙니다. \v 3 그들은 하나님의 의를 알지 못하고 자기 자신의 [의를] 세우려고 힘쓰면서, 하나님의 의에 복종하지 않았습니다.
ko.B: 나는 그들이 하나님을 위한 열심을 품고 있다고 증언할 수 있습니다. 그러나 그 열심은 바른 깨달음에서 나온 것이 아닙니다. \v 3 그들은 하나님의 의를 알지 못했고, 자기 자신의 의를 세우려고 애쓰다가 하나님께서 주시는 의에 복종하지 않았습니다.
ko.R: 나는 그들이 하나님을 섬기는 일에 무척 열심이라는 것을 압니다. 그러나 그들은 제대로 알지 못합니다. \v 3 그들은 하나님의 의, 곧 하나님께서 사람들을 자신과 바른 관계로 세우시는 일을 알지 못했습니다. 그 대신 그들은 자기 힘으로 의를 이루려고 했습니다. 그래서 그들은 하나님께서 주시는 의를 받아들이지 않았습니다.

vi.L: Vì tôi làm chứng cho họ rằng họ có lòng nhiệt thành với Đức Chúa Trời, nhưng không theo sự hiểu biết [đúng đắn]. \v 3 Vì không biết sự công chính của Đức Chúa Trời, và tìm cách lập sự [công chính] riêng [của mình], họ đã không thuận phục sự công chính của Đức Chúa Trời.
vi.B: Tôi có thể làm chứng cho họ rằng họ nhiệt thành với Đức Chúa Trời, nhưng lòng nhiệt thành ấy không dựa trên sự hiểu biết đúng đắn. \v 3 Họ không nhận biết sự công chính của Đức Chúa Trời, và vì cố lập nên một sự công chính riêng cho mình, họ đã không chịu thuận phục sự công chính đến từ Đức Chúa Trời.
vi.R: Tôi có thể nói với anh chị em rằng họ rất hăng hái phục vụ Đức Chúa Trời. Nhưng họ không thật sự hiểu biết. \v 3 Họ không biết về sự công chính của Đức Chúa Trời, tức là cách Đức Chúa Trời làm cho con người được đúng đắn với chính {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Thay vào đó, họ cố tạo cho mình một sự công chính riêng. Vì vậy họ không chịu nhận sự công chính mà Đức Chúa Trời ban.

decisions.choice: zeal for God: eager devotion to God
decisions.reason: ζῆλος is burning eagerness. Paul knew it from the inside: he had been zealous for the traditions of his fathers and had persecuted the church (Galatians 1:13-14, Philippians 3:6).

decisions.choice: knowledge that rightly understands
decisions.reason: ἐπίγνωσις is knowledge that recognizes the truth (as in 1:28). Israel did not lack information; what was missing was a right understanding of what God was doing, which verse 3 explains.

decisions.choice: the righteousness of God: God's own way of putting people right with himself, which he gives
alternatives: God's own justice as a quality of God
decisions.reason: As in 1:17 and 3:21-22, God's righteousness is God acting to put people right, received by faith. It stands against "their own", a righteousness of their own based on the law, as Paul says of himself in Philippians 3:9.

decisions.choice: they did not submit themselves
decisions.reason: ὑπετάγησαν is passive in form but has the sense of submitting oneself, as often with this verb. Not submitting means refusing to accept God's way and trusting their own instead.

decisions.choice: eager to serve God; how God puts people right with himself; the righteousness God gives
decisions.reason: Readable explains "zeal for God" and "the righteousness of God" as meaning notes m1 and m3 describe, as Romans 1:17 does at Readable. Reviewers should check that the explanation does not narrow the phrase.

decisions.choice: the righteousness that comes from God
decisions.reason: Balanced varies the repeated phrase in the second half of verse 3 so that the long sentence reads naturally; it keeps the sense of meaning note m3.

decisions.choice: bidii
decisions.reason: ζῆλον is eager devotion (meaning note m1). Swahili "wivu" now means jealousy and is kept for the related verb in verse 19 ("nitawafanya mwone wivu"); "bidii" (earnest zeal) is the positive sense here. Readable says "hamu kubwa ya kumtumikia Mungu", as the English Readable explains.

decisions.choice: every French pronoun for God or Christ carries the deity_pronoun span, subject "il" included (for this chapter)
decisions.reason: French must write the subject pronoun, so "il" for God or Christ carries the span wherever the English "he" does, and also where French needs an object pronoun the English lacks ("{{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}invoquent", "Dieu {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}a ressuscité"). When God speaks of himself in the quotations, "me", "m’", "mes" and "moi" carry it; "je" does not. A pronoun at the start of a sentence is written plainly with its capital.

decisions.choice: passé composé for past events at every level (for this chapter)
alternatives: passé simple at Literal and Balanced
decisions.reason: Romans is a letter in which Paul argues with his readers, and spoken French tells past events in the passé composé ("ils ne se sont pas soumis", "ils n’ont pas tous obéi"). The passé simple of written narrative would sound like storytelling.

decisions.choice: "하나님의 의" at every level, with Readable adding "하나님께서 사람들을 자신과 바른 관계로 세우시는 일"; "하나님께서 주시는 의" (B, R) the second time
decisions.reason: As settled at 1:17 for the whole letter. The meaning decision reads it as God's way of putting people right with himself, which he gives; Balanced and Readable say "which God gives" the second time, as the English Balanced does.

decisions.choice: "복종하다" (L, B); "받아들이다" (R)
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used of submitting to an authority (13:1); Readable says plainly that they would not accept what God gives.

decisions.choice: "lòng nhiệt thành", "nhiệt thành" (L, B); "hăng hái" (R)
decisions.reason: Zeal for God is eager devotion to him (m1). "Nhiệt thành" is that warm devotion; "ghen" would be heard as jealousy, which is a different sense of the same Greek word (10:19, 11:11). Readable says "hăng hái" (keen), the everyday word.

decisions.choice: "thuận phục" (L, B); "không chịu nhận" (R)
decisions.reason: The verb is to place oneself under (m4): they did not submit themselves. "Thuận phục" is to submit willingly; "vâng phục" is kept for obeying (1:5, 10:16). Readable says they would not accept what God gives, as the English Readable does.

source.text: τέλος γὰρ νόμου Χριστὸς εἰς δικαιοσύνην παντὶ τῷ πιστεύοντι.

records.literal_gloss: End for of law [is] Christ unto righteousness to everyone the believing.

en.L: For {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} [is the] end of [the] law for righteousness to everyone who believes.
en.B: For {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} is the end of the law, bringing righteousness to everyone who believes.
en.R: {{christos:Christ|The Messiah}} is the end of the law. Through {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, everyone who believes can be righteous before God.

es.L: Porque {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}} [es el] fin de [la] ley para justicia a todo el que cree.
es.B: Porque {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}} es el fin de la ley, y trae justicia a todo el que cree.
es.R: {{christos:Cristo|El Mesías}} es el fin de la ley. Por medio de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, todo el que cree puede ser justo delante de Dios.

sw.L: Kwa maana {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} [ndiye] mwisho wa sheria kwa ajili ya haki kwa kila mtu anayeamini.
sw.B: Kwa maana {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} ndiye mwisho wa sheria, akileta haki kwa kila mtu anayeamini.
sw.R: {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} ndiye mwisho wa sheria. Kupitia {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}}, kila mtu anayeamini anaweza kuwa mwenye haki mbele za Mungu.

fr.L: Car {{christos:Christ|le Messie}} [est la] fin de [la] Loi, pour [la] justice de quiconque croit.
fr.B: Car {{christos:Christ|le Messie}} est la fin de la Loi, et ainsi la justice est donnée à quiconque croit.
fr.R: {{christos:Christ|Le Messie}} est la fin de la Loi. Grâce à {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, quiconque croit peut être juste devant Dieu.

ko.L: 율법의 마침은 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}이시니, 믿는 모든 사람이 의에 이르게 [하십니다].
ko.B: {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}께서는 율법의 마침이 되셔서, 믿는 모든 사람에게 의를 가져다주십니다.
ko.R: {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}께서는 율법의 마침이 되셨습니다. 이제 율법은 의에 이르는 길이 아닙니다. 누구든지 그분을 믿으면, 그분을 통해 하나님 앞에서 의로운 사람이 될 수 있습니다.

vi.L: Vì {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}} [là] điểm kết thúc của luật pháp, để [ban] sự công chính cho mọi người tin.
vi.B: Vì {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}} là điểm kết thúc của luật pháp, đem sự công chính đến cho mọi người tin.
vi.R: {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}} là điểm kết thúc của luật pháp. Nhờ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, mọi người tin đều có thể trở nên công chính trước mặt Đức Chúa Trời.

decisions.choice: end: the law has come to its end as the way to righteousness
alternatives: goal: the law was always pointing to Christ
both: the law reaches its goal in Christ and so its end
decisions.reason: τέλος can mean an end, a goal, or an outcome. The contrast in verses 3-6 between a righteousness of one's own from the law and the righteousness from faith favors "end": in Christ the law is no longer the way to be right with God. But Paul has just said that Israel pursued the law and did not reach it (9:31), and he says the law itself bears witness to God's righteousness (3:21, 3:31), which favors "goal". A word for "end" that also allows "goal" keeps both readings open.

decisions.choice: the result: righteousness for everyone who believes
alternatives: a limit on "end": Christ ends the law as a means to righteousness
decisions.reason: The phrase "for righteousness" may say what Christ brings (righteousness for every believer), or in what respect the law has ended (as a way to righteousness). Both readings say that righteousness now comes to everyone who believes; the levels follow the first.

decisions.choice: the law: the law of Moses
decisions.reason: There is no article, but the law in view is the law Israel pursued (9:31) and that Moses wrote (verse 5).

decisions.choice: Through him ... can be righteous before God
decisions.reason: Readable makes the short phrase into a clause and says who brings it; "before God" says where righteousness counts.

decisions.choice: la Loi, with a capital, for the law of Moses at every level (for this chapter)
decisions.reason: The French style guide writes "la Loi" for the law of Moses, which the meaning decision says is meant here and in 10:5. The capital tells French readers that a particular law is meant, not law in general, as English readers learn from the context.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|le Messie}} where the Greek has Christ without the article
decisions.reason: French cannot say "Messie" without an article as a name, while "Christ" is used as a name without one, so the article goes inside the setting span and each option reads naturally.

decisions.choice: "마침" at every level for the end of the law; Readable adds "이제 율법은 의에 이르는 길이 아닙니다"
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads "end" as the law's coming to an end as the way to righteousness, and footnotes the reading "goal". "마침" says that something has come to its close, and can still carry a hint of completion; "목표" would choose the other reading.

decisions.choice: "그분을 통해 하나님 앞에서 의로운 사람이 될 수 있습니다" (R)
decisions.reason: Readable spells out what "for righteousness" means, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "điểm kết thúc" at every level
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads the word as the end of the law as a way to righteousness, with a footnote for "goal". "Điểm kết thúc" says end plainly; "cứu cánh" would choose the footnoted sense of goal. "Sự cuối cùng" is the wording of the 1926 version and is not clear modern Vietnamese.

source.text: Μωϋσῆς γὰρ γράφει ὅτι τὴν δικαιοσύνην τὴν ἐκ τοῦ νόμου ὁ ποιήσας ἄνθρωπος ζήσεται ἐν αὐτῇ.

records.literal_gloss: Moses for writes that the righteousness the from the law: the [one] having done [it] man will live by it.

en.L: For Moses writes [about] the righteousness that [is] from the law, that the {{gender:person|man}} who has done [it] will live by it.
en.B: Moses writes this about the righteousness that comes from the law: "The {{gender:person|man}} who does it will live by it."
en.R: Moses writes about the righteousness that comes from keeping the law. He says, "The {{gender:person|man}} who does what the law commands will live by doing it."

es.L: Porque Moisés escribe [acerca de] la justicia que [es] por la ley, que {{gender:la persona|el hombre}} que [la] practique vivirá por ella.
es.B: Moisés escribe así acerca de la justicia que viene de la ley: «{{gender:La persona|El hombre}} que la practique vivirá por ella».
es.R: Moisés escribe acerca de la justicia que viene de cumplir la ley. Dice: «{{gender:La persona|El hombre}} que hace lo que la ley manda vivirá por hacerlo».

sw.L: Kwa maana Musa anaandika [kuhusu] haki itokayo katika sheria, kwamba mtu aliyeitenda ataishi kwayo.
sw.B: Musa anaandika hivi kuhusu haki inayotokana na sheria: "Mtu anayeitenda ataishi kwayo."
sw.R: Musa anaandika kuhusu haki inayopatikana kwa kushika sheria. Anasema, "Mtu anayefanya yale ambayo sheria inaamuru ataishi kwa kuyafanya."

fr.L: Car Moïse écrit, [au sujet de] la justice qui [vient] de la Loi, que {{gender:l’être humain|l’homme}} qui [l’]aura pratiquée vivra par elle.
fr.B: Moïse écrit ceci à propos de la justice qui vient de la Loi : « {{gender:L’être humain|L’homme}} qui la pratique vivra par elle. »
fr.R: Moïse écrit au sujet de la justice qui vient de l’obéissance à la Loi. Il dit : « {{gender:L’être humain|L’homme}} qui fait ce que la Loi commande vivra en le faisant. »

ko.L: 모세는 율법에서 [나는] 의에 대하여 이렇게 기록합니다. "그것을 행한 사람은 그것으로 살 것이다."
ko.B: 모세는 율법에서 오는 의에 대해 이렇게 기록합니다. "그것을 행하는 사람은 그것으로 살 것이다."
ko.R: 모세는 율법을 지켜서 얻는 의에 대해 이렇게 기록했습니다. "율법이 명령하는 것을 행하는 사람은 그렇게 행함으로써 살 것이다."

vi.L: Vì Môi-se viết về sự công chính [đến] từ luật pháp rằng: người đã làm [những điều ấy] sẽ sống bởi nó.
vi.B: Môi-se viết về sự công chính đến từ luật pháp như sau: "Người nào làm điều đó sẽ nhờ đó mà sống."
vi.R: Môi-se viết về sự công chính đến từ việc giữ luật pháp. Ông nói: "Người nào làm theo những gì luật pháp truyền dạy sẽ nhờ làm như vậy mà được sống."

decisions.choice: Leviticus 18:5
decisions.reason: In Leviticus 18:5 God tells Israel to keep his statutes and rules, for the person who does them will live by them. Paul quotes the same verse in Galatians 3:12. Here he uses it to describe the way of righteousness based on doing.

decisions.choice: "will live by it" (by the righteousness)
alternatives: "will live by them" (by the commandments), with the word order changed, as in Leviticus
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT has "by it", referring to the righteousness. Many manuscripts have "them", the reading of Leviticus 18:5, and place "that" differently. The meaning is close either way. Reviewers must check the apparatus.

decisions.choice: the principle of law-righteousness: life depends on doing
alternatives: a promise Paul rejects as false
decisions.reason: Paul does not deny what Leviticus says. He sets it beside the righteousness from faith (verse 6): righteousness from the law depends on doing what it commands, and no one is put right with God that way (3:20).

decisions.choice: from keeping the law; what the law commands; by doing it
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what "from the law" and "does it" mean.

decisions.choice: the quotation in 해라체 ("살 것이다"), as settled at 2:24; "사람" with no gender span
decisions.reason: Quotations of Scripture are in 해라체 through the letter. "사람" already includes men and women, so the English gender span has no Korean counterpart.

decisions.choice: "người", "người nào" with no gender span
decisions.reason: Vietnamese "người" does not mark sex, so the English gender setting has nothing to choose between here, as in 2:1.

source.text: ἡ δὲ ἐκ πίστεως δικαιοσύνη οὕτως λέγει· Μὴ εἴπῃς ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ σου· Τίς ἀναβήσεται εἰς τὸν οὐρανόν; τοῦτ’ ἔστιν Χριστὸν καταγαγεῖν·

records.literal_gloss: The but from faith righteousness thus speaks: Not you should say in the heart of you: Who will ascend into the heaven? That is, Christ to bring down;

en.L: But the righteousness [that is] from faith speaks thus: "Do not say in your heart, 'Who will ascend into heaven?'" (that is, to bring {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} down);
en.B: But the righteousness that comes from faith speaks like this: "Do not say in your heart, 'Who will go up into heaven?'" (that is, to bring {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} down).
en.R: But the righteousness that comes by faith speaks in a different way. It says, "Do not say to yourself, 'Who will go up to heaven?'" Asking that would mean someone has to go up and bring {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} down.

es.L: Pero la justicia [que es] por la fe dice así: «No digas en tu corazón: “¿Quién subirá al cielo?”» (esto es, para hacer bajar {{christos:a Cristo|al Mesías}});
es.B: Pero la justicia que viene de la fe habla así: «No digas en tu corazón: “¿Quién subirá al cielo?”» (es decir, para hacer bajar {{christos:a Cristo|al Mesías}}).
es.R: Pero la justicia que viene por la fe habla de otra manera. Dice: «No te digas a ti mismo: “¿Quién subirá al cielo?”». Preguntar eso sería como decir que alguien tiene que subir y hacer bajar {{christos:a Cristo|al Mesías}}.

sw.L: Lakini haki itokayo katika imani inasema hivi: "Usiseme ndani ya moyo wako, 'Nani atapanda kwenda mbinguni?'" (yaani, kumshusha {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}});
sw.B: Lakini haki inayotokana na imani inasema hivi: "Usiseme moyoni mwako, 'Ni nani atakayepanda juu mbinguni?'" (yaani, ili kumleta {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} chini).
sw.R: Lakini haki inayopatikana kwa imani inasema kwa namna tofauti. Inasema, "Usijiulize, 'Ni nani atakayepanda kwenda mbinguni?'" Kuuliza hivyo kungemaanisha kwamba mtu lazima apande juu amshushe {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}.

fr.L: Mais la justice [qui vient] de [la] foi parle ainsi : « Ne dis pas dans ton cœur : “Qui montera au ciel ?” » (c’est-à-dire pour faire descendre {{christos:Christ|le Messie}}) ;
fr.B: Mais la justice qui vient de la foi parle ainsi : « Ne dis pas dans ton cœur : “Qui montera au ciel ?” » (c’est-à-dire pour en faire descendre {{christos:Christ|le Messie}}).
fr.R: Mais la justice qui vient par la foi parle autrement. Elle dit : « Ne te dis pas : “Qui va monter au ciel ?” » Poser cette question, ce serait dire que quelqu’un doit monter au ciel pour en faire descendre {{christos:Christ|le Messie}}.

ko.L: 그러나 믿음에서 [나는] 의는 이렇게 말합니다. "너는 네 마음속으로 '누가 하늘로 올라가겠느냐?' 하고 말하지 마라." (곧 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}를 모셔 내리려는 것입니다.)
ko.B: 그러나 믿음에서 오는 의는 이렇게 말합니다. "너는 마음속으로 '누가 하늘에 올라가겠느냐?' 하고 말하지 마라." (그것은 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}를 모셔 내려오겠다는 말과 같습니다.)
ko.R: 그러나 믿음으로 얻는 의는 다르게 말합니다. "너는 속으로 '누가 하늘에 올라가겠느냐?' 하고 말하지 마라." 그렇게 묻는 것은, 누군가가 하늘에 올라가서 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}를 모셔 내려와야 한다는 뜻이 됩니다.

vi.L: Nhưng sự công chính [đến] từ đức tin nói thế này: "Đừng nói trong lòng bạn: 'Ai sẽ lên trời?'" (tức là để đem {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}} xuống);
vi.B: Nhưng sự công chính đến từ đức tin thì nói thế này: "Đừng nói trong lòng mình: 'Ai sẽ lên trời?'" (nghĩa là để đem {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}} xuống).
vi.R: Nhưng sự công chính đến bởi đức tin thì nói một cách khác: "Đừng tự hỏi: 'Ai sẽ lên trời?'" Hỏi như vậy có nghĩa là phải có người lên trời để đem {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}} xuống.

decisions.choice: the question and Paul's comment on it are one record
alternatives: "that is, to bring Christ down" as a sentence on its own, as the SBLGNT's question mark allows
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT ends the quoted question with a question mark, but the next words, τοῦτ ἔστιν ("that is"), are Paul's comment on that question and cannot stand alone. The record keeps them together; the meaning is the same either way.

decisions.choice: Deuteronomy 30:12, with "Do not say in your heart" from Deuteronomy 9:4
decisions.reason: In Deuteronomy 30:11-14 Moses tells Israel that God's command is not too hard or far away: it is not in heaven, so that someone must go up and fetch it, nor beyond the sea, but very near. "Do not say in your heart" comes from Deuteronomy 9:4, a warning against thinking that Israel earned the land by its own righteousness. Paul lets the righteousness from faith speak in Moses' words.

decisions.choice: the righteousness from faith speaks, as if a person
decisions.reason: Paul sets two voices side by side: Moses writing about law-righteousness (verse 5) and the righteousness from faith speaking for itself. The word "but" marks the contrast.

decisions.choice: say in your heart: think to yourself
decisions.reason: In the Old Testament, to say something in one's heart is to think it privately (Psalm 14:1).

decisions.choice: as if Christ had not already come down from heaven
alternatives: as if a person had to climb to heaven to find righteousness
decisions.reason: Paul's comment, "that is", applies the question to Christ. To ask who will go up to heaven would be to act as though Christ still had to be brought down, when he has already come. Righteousness does not have to be fetched; God has brought it near.

decisions.choice: Asking that would mean someone has to go up and bring the Messiah down
alternatives: that is, to bring Christ down
decisions.reason: Readable spells out what Paul's short comment means (meaning note m5).

decisions.choice: speaks in a different way
decisions.reason: Readable makes the contrast with verse 5 explicit.

decisions.choice: the words of Deuteronomy in 해라체 with "너" ("말하지 마라"); Paul's comment in 합쇼체
decisions.reason: The personified righteousness speaks in the words of Scripture, which are in 해라체 through the letter; Paul's own explanation keeps the letter's 합쇼체, so the two voices stay apart.

decisions.choice: "{{christos:그리스도|메시아}}를 모셔 내리다" (L); "모셔 내려오다" (B, R), with the humble verb "모시다"
decisions.reason: Korean shows respect for the person brought, so bringing Christ down or up is said with "모시다"; the same in verse 7.

decisions.choice: "마음속으로 ... 말하다" (L, B); "속으로 ... 말하다" (R)
decisions.reason: "Say in your heart" means think to yourself (meaning decision); Korean "마음속으로 말하다" keeps the picture and is still clear.

decisions.choice: "bạn" for the singular "you" in 10:6-9
decisions.reason: The singular "you" of Deuteronomy is spoken by the righteousness from faith (m3), and in verse 9 Paul applies it to each reader. As in 2:1 and 8:2, the singular reader is "bạn"; "ngươi" is kept for God's own words in Old Testament quotations (9:17, 9:26), and "anh chị em" would make it plural.

decisions.choice: "Đừng tự hỏi" (R); "nói trong lòng mình" (B)
decisions.reason: To say in one's heart is to think to oneself (m4). Balanced keeps the picture, which Vietnamese also uses; Readable says "ask yourself", which fits the question that follows.

source.text: ἤ· Τίς καταβήσεται εἰς τὴν ἄβυσσον; τοῦτ’ ἔστιν Χριστὸν ἐκ νεκρῶν ἀναγαγεῖν.

records.literal_gloss: Or: Who will descend into the abyss? That is, Christ out of dead to bring up.

en.L: or, "Who will descend into the abyss?" (that is, to bring {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} up from [the] dead).
en.B: Or, "Who will go down into the abyss?" (that is, to bring {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} back up from the dead).
en.R: Or, "Who will go down into the deep, to the place of the dead?" Asking that would mean someone has to go down and bring {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} back from the dead.

es.L: o: «¿Quién descenderá al abismo?» (esto es, para hacer subir {{christos:a Cristo|al Mesías}} de entre [los] muertos).
es.B: O: «¿Quién bajará al abismo?» (es decir, para hacer volver {{christos:a Cristo|al Mesías}} de entre los muertos).
es.R: O: «¿Quién bajará a lo profundo, al lugar de los muertos?». Preguntar eso sería como decir que alguien tiene que bajar y traer {{christos:a Cristo|al Mesías}} de vuelta de entre los muertos.

sw.L: au, "Nani atashuka kwenda kuzimu?" (yaani, kumpandisha {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} kutoka kwa wafu).
sw.B: Au, "Ni nani atakayeshuka kuzimu?" (yaani, ili kumrudisha {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} juu kutoka kwa wafu).
sw.R: Au, "Ni nani atakayeshuka chini kuzimu, mahali pa wafu?" Kuuliza hivyo kungemaanisha kwamba mtu lazima ashuke amrudishe {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} kutoka kwa wafu.

fr.L: ou : « Qui descendra dans l’abîme ? » (c’est-à-dire pour faire remonter {{christos:Christ|le Messie}} d’entre [les] morts).
fr.B: Ou : « Qui descendra dans l’abîme ? » (c’est-à-dire pour faire remonter {{christos:Christ|le Messie}} d’entre les morts).
fr.R: Ou bien : « Qui va descendre dans les profondeurs, au pays des morts ? » Poser cette question, ce serait dire que quelqu’un doit y descendre pour ramener {{christos:Christ|le Messie}} d’entre les morts.

ko.L: 또는 "누가 깊은 구렁으로 내려가겠느냐?" (곧 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}를 죽은 사람들 가운데서 모셔 올리려는 것입니다.)
ko.B: 또 "누가 깊은 구렁으로 내려가겠느냐?" 하는 말도 그렇습니다. (그것은 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}를 죽은 사람들 가운데서 다시 모셔 올리겠다는 말과 같습니다.)
ko.R: 또 "누가 깊은 곳, 곧 죽은 사람들이 있는 곳으로 내려가겠느냐?" 하고 말하지 마라. 그렇게 묻는 것은, 누군가가 그곳에 내려가서 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}를 죽음에서 다시 모셔 와야 한다는 뜻이 됩니다.

vi.L: hoặc: "Ai sẽ xuống vực sâu?" (tức là để đem {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}} lên từ [giữa] kẻ chết).
vi.B: Hoặc: "Ai sẽ xuống vực sâu?" (nghĩa là để đem {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}} từ cõi chết trở lên).
vi.R: Hoặc: "Ai sẽ xuống vực sâu, là nơi của người chết?" Hỏi như vậy có nghĩa là phải có người xuống đó để đem {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}} từ cõi chết trở về.

decisions.choice: the question and Paul's comment on it are one record
alternatives: "that is, to bring Christ up from the dead" as a sentence on its own
decisions.reason: As in verse 6, the SBLGNT ends the question with a question mark, but Paul's comment that follows cannot stand alone.

decisions.choice: Deuteronomy 30:13, reworded
alternatives: a new saying of Paul's own
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy 30:13 asks who will cross the sea to bring the command back. Paul has "go down into the abyss" instead. In the Old Testament the deep of the sea and the depths below the earth are pictures of death, from which God brings his people up again (Psalm 71:20, Jonah 2:2-6), so the change fits Paul's point about Christ rising from the dead.

decisions.choice: the abyss: the depths, the place of the dead
decisions.reason: ἄβυσσος is the deep, used in the Greek Old Testament for the depths of the sea and of the earth. Paul's comment, "to bring Christ up from the dead", shows that he means the place of the dead.

decisions.choice: as if Christ had not already been raised
decisions.reason: To ask who will go down to the dead would be to act as though Christ had not already been raised by God. Both his coming and his rising are done; nothing is left for people to do to bring him near.

decisions.choice: to the place of the dead; Asking that would mean someone has to go down
decisions.reason: Readable explains "the abyss" (meaning note m3) and spells out Paul's comment as in verse 6.

decisions.choice: kuzimu
decisions.reason: "Kuzimu" is the world below, the place of the dead, which is what Paul means by the abyss (meaning note m3). "Vilindi" (the depths of the sea) would keep the picture from Deuteronomy but not Paul's point, and "shimo lisilo na mwisho" (bottomless pit) suggests the abyss of Revelation.

decisions.choice: "깊은 구렁" (L, B); "깊은 곳, 곧 죽은 사람들이 있는 곳" (R)
decisions.reason: As for the same word in Luke 8:31. "무저갱" is the older church word and is hard for most readers; the meaning decision says the abyss here is the place of the dead, which Readable says.

decisions.choice: "vực sâu" at every level, with "là nơi của người chết" (R)
decisions.reason: The abyss is the depths, the place of the dead (m3). "Vực sâu" keeps the picture of depth set against heaven in verse 6; "âm phủ" would name Hades, a different word. Readable adds what the depths are, as the English Readable does.

records.literal_gloss: But what says it?

en.L: But what does it say?
en.B: But what does it say?
en.R: So what does it say?

es.L: Pero ¿qué dice?
es.B: Pero ¿qué dice?
es.R: Entonces, ¿qué dice?

sw.L: Lakini inasema nini?
sw.B: Lakini inasema nini?
sw.R: Basi, inasema nini?

fr.L: Mais que dit-elle ?
fr.B: Mais que dit-elle ?
fr.R: Alors, que dit-elle ?

ko.L: 그러나 그것은 무엇이라고 말합니까?
ko.B: 그렇다면 그것은 무엇이라고 말합니까?
ko.R: 그렇다면 믿음으로 얻는 의는 무엇이라고 말합니까?
